children: The Philippines' Anti-Money Laundering Council has obtained a court freeze order covering more than 100 financial accounts and other assets linked to a lawmaker and several individuals and entities. According to ChainCatcher, the assets are suspected of being tied to corruption, plunder, and irregularities in flood control projects.

The freeze covers 86 bank accounts, four investment accounts, one insurance policy, and 25 virtual asset wallets. The AMLC said funds moved through multiple virtual asset service providers and several virtual asset wallets, making them harder to trace. The council did not disclose the identities of the lawmaker or the other parties involved.

title: Philippines Freezes Over 100 Accounts and Assets in Corruption Probe
